product: MiniMax Speech / T2A v2 (speech-2.8-hd, speech-2.8-turbo, speech-2.6, speech-02, speech-01 families)
recut_note: Re-cut onto the corrected frame after Tom's course correction of 2026-08-26 11:06Z: Welsh is OUT (human-recorded), coverage is counted against the three tiers of languages that actually use TTS, and TTS is a BRIDGE to human recording, so exit cost is scored alongside entry cost. The vendor research below is unchanged and every source citation is the original one; the frame around it is new. Companion dossier: docs/tts-bakeoff/gate-zero-candidates-recut-2026-08-26.md

headline.one_line: Middling coverage, the best timestamp story of the hosted three, and the worst licensing position of any candidate — the readable MiniMax terms grant MiniMax a perpetual irrevocable licence over uploaded content, which is the exact thing this project exists to avoid.
headline.tier_coverage: Tier A 8/10 (misses ben — live, 20,315 clips — and glg — live, 15,931 clips). Tier B 10/11 (misses pdc only). Tier A+B+C 31/44.
headline.discriminator: Not coverage: ties at 10/11 on Tier B like everyone else. MiniMax's distinguishing facts are (a) it is the only hosted candidate with word-level timing on the batch path (subtitle_enable, subtitle type word), (b) it can render native 44.1 kHz mp3 up to 256 kbps, matching the house master, and (c) it is the weakest on both version pinning (floating model names, no dated snapshots, no deprecation policy) and licensing.
headline.verdict: WEAK CANDIDATE, WORST BRIDGE. The licence problem is not paperwork: SSi is leaving xAI so that Aran's voice does not feed a company the founders object to, and MiniMax's readable terms take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence over user content that expressly survives termination. Recommend dropping unless the API platform terms — which could not be read, see gaps — say something materially different.

sources.title: Text to Speech (T2A) HTTP — MiniMax API Docs
sources.what_it_established: The verbatim language_boost enum (41 values plus auto, Welsh absent); the full live model list speech-2.8-hd/turbo, 2.6-hd/turbo, 02-hd/turbo, 01-hd/turbo; voice_setting parameters speed 0.5-2, vol 0-10, pitch -12..+12 and nine emotions; a pronunciation dictionary exists; NO seed and NO temperature parameter; rate-limit error codes 1002 and 1039 (TPM) exist but thresholds are not published.

sources.title: Voice Clone — MiniMax API Docs
sources.what_it_established: Source audio minimum 10 seconds, maximum 5 minutes, mp3/m4a/wav, up to 20 MB; optional example audio under 8 seconds. NO consent requirement, NO verification, NO statement about the right to clone another person's voice appears in the documentation.

sources.title: MiniMax Speech 2.5 launch announcement
sources.what_it_established: Claims 40+ languages and names the additions (Bulgarian, Danish, Greek, Swedish, Filipino, Hungarian, Spanish, Finnish, Norwegian, Slovak, Swahili, Catalan, Lithuanian, Afrikaans). Welsh is not mentioned. Claims cross-lingual cloning preserves speaker identity and accent across languages — a marketing claim, not a spec.

sources.title: MiniMax subscription pricing
sources.what_it_established: Five tiers from Starter $5/mo to Business $999/mo, 100,000 to 20,000,000 monthly audio points, 10 to 800 voice slots, RPM 10 to 800. Per-character rates and voice-cloning cost are NOT published on this page.

welsh_footnote.evidence: language_boost is a closed enum and its 41 values are, verbatim: Chinese, Chinese,Yue, English, Arabic, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, German, Turkish, Dutch, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Japanese, Italian, Korean, Thai, Polish, Romanian, Greek, Czech, Finnish, Hindi, Bulgarian, Danish, Hebrew, Malay, Persian, Slovak, Swedish, Croatian, Filipino, Hungarian, Norwegian, Slovenian, Catalan, Nynorsk, Tamil, Afrikaans, plus auto. No Welsh. The Speech 2.5 launch post enumerates the newly added languages and Welsh is not among them either.
welsh_footnote.rationale: Absent from a closed enum, so MiniMax is DEAD as a stock-Welsh provider — the same position as Cartesia. It stays CONDITIONAL on the same single empirical question, with one wrinkle in its favour and one against. In its favour: language_boost accepts 'auto', so unlike a hard language field there is a documented way to submit text without asserting a language, which is exactly the shape of request a Welsh probe would need; and MiniMax's own cross-lingual cloning claim is the most aggressive of the four ('cross-lingual cloning is no longer a challenge'), which is precisely the property that would carry Aran's north-Welsh or Catrin's south-Welsh into an unlisted language. Against: that claim is a launch-post assertion with no benchmark behind it, and 'auto' language detection on a language the model was never trained on will most likely fall back to English or Irish-adjacent phonetics and produce Welsh with an English mouth. The dialect question is the same as everywhere: no vendor addresses north versus south Welsh, so the only route is that a clone carries its speaker's own dialect. Settle it in phase 2 with a paid probe: clone Aran from 10s-5min of audio, render 20 Welsh course seeds with language_boost auto, have a Welsh speaker score them. Note this is the candidate where the probe is cheapest per attempt and the consent story is weakest.
welsh_footnote.demoted_because: Welsh is done by human recording (cym_n_for_eng / cym_s_for_eng are 96.4% human, the only human-voiced language in the estate). Vendor Welsh support does not decide this evaluation. Kept verbatim because it is the only yardstick we have for a vendor's reach into Welsh, which will matter if the human-recording programme ever needs a synthetic stand-in. The gate_zero verdict inside this block is SUPERSEDED and must not be quoted as a live verdict.

exit_cost.verdict: HARD — the hardest of the four, and hard for the specific reason this project exists.
exit_cost.score_rationale: MiniMax is technically the easiest hosted vendor to get boundary data and matching audio out of, and contractually the worst place to have put Aran's voice. The readable MiniMax terms take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence over user content that expressly survives termination. Deleting a voice_id does not undo a perpetual licence over the audio that created it.

boundary_data.available: YES — word-level, on the batch path.
boundary_data.detail: subtitle_enable (default false) turns on subtitles, with subtitle types sentence, word and word_streaming. The response carries subtitle_file, 'Download link for generated subtitles… timestamped in milliseconds, returned in JSON format'. This is the only hosted candidate offering word timings on the ordinary batch endpoint rather than on a streaming one — operationally the best fit for a bulk course render of the four.
boundary_data.catch: The same doc paragraph describes subtitles as 'aligned to sentences (≤ 50 characters)' while the type enum offers word and word_streaming, so the exact granularity of what actually comes back is ambiguous on paper and needs one paid probe to settle. And it arrives as a download URL, not inline, so a bulk render needs a fetch-and-store step and the link's expiry is undocumented.

audio_format.containers: mp3, pcm, flac, wav, pcmu_raw, pcmu_wav, opus
audio_format.fits_house_master: YES — 44.1 kHz native, mp3 up to 256 kbps, so no upsample and no bandwidth ceiling beside a human recording. Level with Cartesia, ahead of OpenAI and Chatterbox on this axis.

licensing_after_we_stop_paying.verdict: BAD, AND THE BAD PART IS THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST TO THIS PROJECT.
licensing_after_we_stop_paying.detail: The readable MiniMax terms state: 'By using the Services, you grant to us, our affiliates, successors, and assigns a royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, non-exclusive right and license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, publish, translate, create derivative works from, distribute, and communicate your User Contributions and User Generated Content' — and the company retains those rights after termination. The same document says 'These Terms of Use permit you to use the Services for your personal, non-commercial use only' and prohibits commercial use of anything available through the Services; commercial rights are attached to paid tiers elsewhere. Read plainly, uploading Aran's voice to MiniMax hands MiniMax a perpetual irrevocable licence to reproduce and create derivative works from it, which cannot be revoked by deleting the voice or closing the account. SSi is leaving xAI precisely so that a founder's voice does not sit inside a company the founders object to; this term reproduces that problem in a different jurisdiction. Nothing in the readable terms addresses what happens to already-generated audio when a subscription lapses.

clone_retirement.mechanism: Delete Voice API — deletes a voice_id created by the Voice Clone or Voice Design APIs. 'Once deleted, the voice_id cannot be reused.'
clone_retirement.detail: Mechanically the clearest deletion statement of the hosted three. Contractually it may be beside the point: the perpetual licence above attaches to the uploaded audio, not to the voice_id, so removing the id does not obviously remove MiniMax's rights over the source recording of Aran's voice. No consent, verification or ownership terms appear anywhere in the voice-cloning documentation, so there is no vendor-side consent artefact to withdraw either.

gaps: THE DECISIVE DOCUMENT COULD NOT BE READ. platform.minimax.io/protocol/terms-of-service — the API platform terms, which are the ones that would actually govern an SSi API contract — renders client-side and returned only a page header. Every licensing statement above is from the App and Web Terms of Service at minimax.io, which may or may not be the governing document for API use. This is the single largest unknown in this candidate and it is a blocker, not a detail: if the platform terms differ materially the verdict could move. It needs either a browser-rendered fetch or MiniMax's own confirmation.
Subtitle granularity is ambiguous in the documentation (sentence-aligned prose against a word-level enum) and the subtitle_file link's expiry is undocumented.
Per-character pricing and per-clone cost remain absent from vendor documentation.
Nothing was measured. There is no MiniMax key on this box.

version_pinning: De facto rather than by policy, and that distinction matters. Eight model ids are simultaneously live — speech-2.8-hd, speech-2.8-turbo, speech-2.6-hd, speech-2.6-turbo, speech-02-hd, speech-02-turbo, speech-01-hd, speech-01-turbo — and model is an explicit request parameter, so you can name an old generation and keep naming it. speech-01 still being callable while 2.8 ships is real evidence of long model lifetimes, and it is the best empirical signal any of the four gives. But there are no DATED snapshots, so 'speech-2.8-hd' is a floating name that MiniMax can retrain underneath us without changing the identifier, and no announcement would be required. No deprecation policy, no notice period and no output-stability guarantee were found anywhere in the documentation. In short: probably stable, provably nothing. For a system whose whole requirement is that a re-render next year sounds like the same person, 'probably' is the wrong word, and this is the axis on which MiniMax is weakest relative to Cartesia and OpenAI.
cloning_consent: MiniMax publishes NO consent requirement, NO verification step and NO statement about the right to clone another person's voice in its voice-cloning documentation. That is not a neutral finding — of the four candidates it is the only one where I could not locate any consent obligation at all, and Tom should read that as a risk rather than as convenience. What it needs technically: 10 seconds to 5 minutes of source audio, mp3/m4a/wav, up to 20 MB, optionally an example clip under 8 seconds. WHAT TO SAY TO ARAN AND CATRIN: MiniMax will not ask them for anything. There is no form, no consent recording, no identity check — we upload audio and a voice exists. So the consent record is entirely ours to create and keep, and they should be told that their voice would be uploaded to a Chinese-platform API whose terms on training-data reuse and voice deletion I could not verify from the documentation. Given this project exists because Tom will not feed Aran's voice to a company he does not want it in, that unverified position is a substantive objection, not a paperwork gap.

controls.seed: Absent. No seed parameter in the T2A API.
controls.other: voice_setting exposes speed (0.5-2), vol (0-10), pitch (-12 to +12) and nine named emotions including happy, sad, angry and whisper. A pronunciation dictionary for custom pronunciation rules is documented, which puts MiniMax ahead of Chatterbox and level with Cartesia on the ability to force a word. language_boost accepts an explicit language or 'auto'.

self_host: No. Hosted API only; no weights, no on-prem offer in the public documentation.
pricing: NOT VERIFIED FROM VENDOR DOCUMENTATION — flagged rather than asserted. The official pricing page publishes subscription tiers (Starter $5/mo to Business $999/mo, 100,000 to 20,000,000 monthly audio points, 10 to 800 voice slots) but no per-character rate and no voice-cloning cost. Third-party sources consistently report roughly $100 per million characters for HD models and $60 per million for Turbo, and roughly $0.50-$1.50 per clone via resellers, but these are not vendor documentation and are recorded here only as an order of magnitude to be confirmed. If those figures hold, MiniMax HD is around three times the price of Cartesia per character.
rate_limits: RPM by tier, from 10 (Starter) to 800 (Business). The API defines rate-limit error code 1002 and a separate TPM-exceeded code 1039, so a token-per-minute ceiling exists, but its value is not published. 10 RPM on the entry tier is far too low for bulk course rendering; the tier would have to be sized to the job.
gaps: No MiniMax API key on this box. Nothing was measured; every figure is documentation or, for pricing, third-party report.
Per-character pricing and per-clone cost are NOT on any vendor documentation page I could reach. The numbers in circulation are third-party and are labelled as such.
TPM thresholds are undocumented — only the error code exists. Cannot size a bulk re-render from published information.

No consent, verification or voice-ownership terms in the cloning docs at all. Whether uploaded voice audio is reused for training is unverified, which for this project specifically is a material unknown rather than a formality.
No dated model snapshots and no published deprecation policy — model ids are floating names that can be retrained underneath us silently.
Documentation is split across minimax.io and minimaxi.com with several published URLs returning 404; the pages that did resolve are the ones cited.
